institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant and interesting courses in english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was very easy to find. NTNU has multiple webpages for international students regarding all needs as a newcomer, both personal and educational. Moreover, NTNU had information meetings, online before the visit and with physical attendance upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, NTNU was very good at assisting in the arrival. They sent out emails before arrival and held meetings before and after arrival. They were also very good at informing us about were to find help, if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
We used
hybel.no
to find rooms for rent. It was very easy, but be aware of renting-companies trying to make you sign absurd contracts, where they will be able to demand more than your deposit after your stay, if they require it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live off campus, as it can give a more reel view into living in Norway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding housing outside of student-housing opportunities was fine, but finding information on SIT and the opportunities through there was very difficult for EU-students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy, I do not remember the exact steps though. But NTNU has a webside, where they help you with every step of the way - even your online-learning agreement.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NTNU webside and email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That was not a problem at all. We got all the courses we wished for. The only thing very different than our home university is that you could change courses up until the 1st of september and the lecturers can change lecture and exam dates "as they please", which they do. So be aware of changes in the beginning.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Regularly check your school email and look at their website for advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both BA and MA courses, which was perfectly fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lecture style was very like that of UCPH, but they did not have the same type of practice classes with questions aw we are used to, which made following the courses more difficult.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MOL3005 - Immunology, MOL3023 - Molecular Medical Bacteriology & NEVR2010 - Introduction to Neuroscience.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all my courses, but be aware that neuroscience is an exclusively online course, with lectures on zoom. This can, however, be an advantage when you are on exchange, as it gives you more flexibility for traveling and exploring the country. The lectures were recorded and uploaded, so it was possible to watch them later.

questions.answer:
Not many unexpected costs, except unnessecary memberships for international students in the beginning. 
But remember to factor in traveling and "fun" expenses.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than i thought, due to the low currency exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every thing you can possibly think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed the SIT-training membership as well as NTNUI, as you could "rent" equipment there for free.
- Both skiing equipment and for other outdoor activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definitely Lofoten, Tromsø, Røros and just in general all of Norway! 
In Trondheim: Ladestien, Bymarka (Gjeitfjellet, Storheia, Elgsæterhytta, Grønlia), Nidarsdomen and the rest of Trondheim.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe joining sports or other social activities/clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That shops are closed on sundays, I kept forgetting.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hiking.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Relax, you will find friends. Everyone is very nice and welcoming and in the same boat as you. Sometimes it just takes a little time to find the exact right ones.
2. Explore the city on foot and try different cafés - coffee is cheap! 
3. Plan trips out of the city and be careful not to have too many visitors from home occupying your weekends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Bring warm clothes and good shoes.
OBS: it gets very slippery when the snow starts to fall!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and trying new things.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping my calm and prioritising the experience over grades.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
